This is the last day of your life.

The sun was in my eyes, and my hands clung to the wheel. The sticky clammy wheel, all gummed up with the remnants of a fast meal. One of many I had eaten, parked in the front seat of my car. The radio turned up, to some obnoxious talk show. The seat enveloped by my large form, straining against gravity to contain it.

Hunger ravished my body; the need to consume, all encompassing. Lights lit up my desire, a thousand sirens calling out to my lone ship, sailing in this sea of cheap fast satisfaction. Grease and sugar, the lover easily obtained. I followed a red sign, calling out to me; the friend my sub conscience gravely followed, whenever it called.

I placed my order for three, safely in the cocoon of my sedan. I swapped plastic for calories, and sat a disposable passenger beside me. My ship set sail, it's lonely voyage continued, the sirens call answered. The sun in my eyes, but a friend beside me. My hands caressed the package, clawing open its riches. Satiating my hunger, quick panicked movements, ravishing the traveller besides me. My attention divided, between the road and my happiness.

My ships course wronged, by the siren aboard. My vessel tacked left, and strayed into the wind; the wind of a metal monster, closing on my small ship. It trumped at my safe little cocoon, threatening to demolish my world, and claw it open; as my hand had done to countless paper packages. Panic lit up my mind, my heart jumped in my chest. Food spilt from my mouth as my arms jerked right. My vessel screeched its disdain, the laws of this world, hampering its struggle, to please my correction.

The monster closed its distance, its great maw open to our embrace. Both ships screeched there complaint, to ever impending doom. My foot hit the brake, delayed between action and thought. Slowly I spun, into its path, the aft of my ship, sunken by force. I spun away, backwards this time, like some cheap fairground ride, white knuckles gripping to the bar that might save me. Onto the verge I spun, adrenaline slowing the show, like some cheap sports commentary.

I couldn't breath with the panic, as adrenaline assaulted my body. It's chemical release crushing my heart, as it strained to pump blood and grease, through corroded arteries. This sharp stabbing, clenching at me from within. The damage of ten thousand fast meals, undoing my heart. My hands clawed at my chest, and gelatinous flesh held them at bay. This crushing feeling, my head spinning, shadows looming in the periphery. The sirens victim, courted over years. My eyes closed, greasy hand marks on my shirt, the remains of my last meal besides me.
